subject: Career
title: The Two-Minute Rule for Remote Focus
description: One-minute skill: The Two-Minute Rule for Remote Focus.

hook.text: A dish in the sink. A laundry pile. At home, tiny tasks scream for attention. Remote workers fight the urge.

buildup.text: David Allen's 'Getting Things Done' principle: if a task takes less than two minutes, do it now.

discovery.text: Quick home tasks — loading the dishwasher, folding a towel — clear mental load without breaking flow.

twist.text: But chains of two-minute tasks become an hour of avoidance. Batch them into breaks, not work time.

climax.text: Set a rule: two-minute tasks during breaks only. During focus blocks, ignore the laundry.

punchline.text: Home is full of small distractions. Rules keep you on track.

quiz.question: What is David Allen's two-minute rule?
options: If a task takes less than two minutes, do it now
Work for only two minutes at a time
Take a break every two minutes

details.summary: David Allen's two-minute rule states that if a task takes less than two minutes, do it immediately rather than adding it to your list. In remote work, strategically batching these micro-tasks prevents them from fragmenting deep focus periods.
details.whyItMatters: Remote workers face a constant stream of small requests via chat and email. Without a strategy for micro-tasks, they accumulate and fragment attention throughout the entire day.
takeaways: Handle two-minute tasks immediately only during designated admin periods
During deep work blocks, capture micro-tasks for later batch processing
The rule works best when combined with time-blocking strategies

faq.question: Should remote workers apply the two-minute rule during deep work sessions?
faq.answer: No. During deep focus periods, capture two-minute tasks in a running list and batch them together during a scheduled admin block. Interrupting deep work for a two-minute task costs far more than two minutes due to the context-switching penalty.

faq.question: How do you batch two-minute tasks effectively when working remotely?
faq.answer: Schedule two to three thirty-minute admin blocks throughout the day specifically for processing quick tasks, responding to Slack messages, and handling email. This batching approach protects focus time while ensuring nothing falls through the cracks.
